outcomes.title: An operator signs in and reaches the control plane
criteria: The dashboard accepts an access token and shows the primary navigation and the Work view

outcomes.title: An operator creates work and finds it where they look
criteria: A created work item is listed in the work list
A created work item appears in the board's backlog group

outcomes.title: An operator reads an item's criteria and gates
criteria: An item's page shows its criteria, proofs and gates by id and by key

outcomes.title: An operator sees what is tested and whether it passes
criteria: The Tests page lists every case with its recent runs

outcomes.title: My change is proven on its own local preview before it can join a candidate
criteria: A change whose declared application cases need a running application is held out of every candidate until its local preview passes
The preview serves this change with its own application state and database and runs the change's declared application cases on it
The team sees the preview requirement and its results recorded with the change in the control plane

outcomes.title: Previews cannot see production data or secrets, and never outlive their run
criteria: Each preview runs against its own application state and database, separate from every other preview and from production
No production secret is available inside a preview
Preview resources are bounded and cleaned up automatically, and the operator can see this on the delivery path

outcomes.title: Our static site and our declared Compose app both get previews, without Railway or GitHub Actions
criteria: A static-site project keeps the preview path it already has, with no second implementation
A project that declares a Compose-backed application gets the same local preview treatment with no Railway requirement
GitHub Actions and Railway are never required for the local preview and candidate path

outcomes.title: Our ready changes travel in small candidates that name exactly what is in them
criteria: At most five ready changes are assembled into one candidate and the rest wait for the next one
A candidate that is not full proceeds after a short configurable wait instead of blocking
Every member is named with its exact source identity (merge SHA) so nothing untested rides along

outcomes.title: Only a candidate whose combined required cases pass is promoted
criteria: A candidate is validated by running the combined required end-to-end cases of every change it carries
The candidate's result and any promotion are bound to its exact source and artifact identities
A failed candidate never promotes and its failure stays recorded with the cases that failed

outcomes.title: What runs in production is verified to be the release that passed
criteria: The live production environment reports the exact release it runs and the control plane matches it to the promoted candidate
The team sees production's verification state with that release identity, turning stale when the live release drifts

outcomes.title: Installing Graphyard on a new repository turns this delivery path on by itself
criteria: Normal project onboarding applies the rapid delivery path by itself: previews when the declared application cases need one, batches of at most five with a short wait, promotion gated on the combined required cases, and production verification
GitHub stays an optional asynchronous mirror under the control-plane merger, and implementation workers receive no trusted proof credentials
The user and operator docs under docs/ describe the defaults, project declarations, local isolation, failure recovery and production verification
